sentences.text: Per contra, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would submit that there are specific allegations made against the Accused No.1.
Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor would further submit that when there are disputed questions of facts, the case cannot be quashed since it is a matter of trial.
Determination by the Court 7.

A bare perusal of Section 482 makes it clear that the Code envisages that inherent powers of the High Court are not limited or affected so as to make orders as may be necessary; (i) to give effect to any order under the Code or, (ii)
to prevent abuse of the process of any Court or, otherwise (iii) to secure ends of justice.
A court while sitting in Section 482 jurisdiction is not functioning as a court of appeal or a court of revision.
It must exercise its powers to do real and substantial justice, depending on the facts and circumstances of the case.
These powers must be invoked for compelling reasons of abuse of process of law or glaring injustice, which are against sound principles of criminal jurisprudence.

The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that  this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over  the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of  implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes,
 without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the  complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from  the said judgments that false implication by way of general  omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute,
 if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the  courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the  husband when no prima facie case is made out against them.
22.Therefore

, upon consideration of the relevant circumstances and in the absence of any specific role attributed to the accused appellants, it would be unjust if the Appellants are forced to go through the tribulations of a trial, i.e., general and omnibus allegations cannot manifest in a situation where the relatives of the complainant's husband are forced to undergo trial.

It has been highlighted by this court in varied instance that a criminal trial leading to an eventual acquittal also inflicts severe scars upon the accused, and such an exercise must therefore be discouraged."
(emphasis supplied)

9. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Achin Gupta v. State of Haryana and 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 141 VJPJ,
another4, highlighted the requirement of taking the realities into consideration and legislating,
especially in the context of the Sections 85 and 86 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita 2023.

The relevant observations made in the context of the present case highlighting the duty of this Court, in the said judgment is as follows;
"25.

If a person is made to face a criminal trial on some general and sweeping allegations without bringing on record any specific instances of criminal conduct, it is nothing but abuse of the process of the court.

The court owes a duty to subject the allegations levelled in the complaint to a thorough scrutiny to find out, prima facie,
whether there is any grain of truth in the allegations or whether they are made only with the sole object of involving certain individuals in a criminal charge, more particularly when a prosecution arises from a matrimonial dispute."
(emphasis supplied)
10.

"The decisions referred above on the subject of exercise of power under Section 482,
Cr.P.C., would undoubtedly cast a duty on the Courts to consider the contentions that there is lack of specific allegations against the accused concerned to constitute the offence(s) alleged against a relative or that the implication was nothing but an over implication to pressurise the family of the husband to yield to the demands.
The Courts cannot refrain from discharging the obligation to consider such contentions.

It appears that in the case on hand despite raising of specific contentions which require deeper consideration, may be taking note of the submissions made on behalf of the complainant that the challan was presented and the matter stood listed for framing charges and hence, it 2024 INSC 369 2024 INSC 896 VJPJ, would be open to accused No.5 to raise all plea at the time of framing of the charges, the Court refrained itself from considering the contentions raised against accused No.5."
(emphasis supplied)

11. To summarize the judgments referred supra, it can be clearly stated that in criminal proceedings arising out of matrimonial matters, when there is no iota or whisper of allegations present In the contents of the complaint, necessary for the ingredients under the Section, general, vague and omnibus allegations and mere casual reference of names of relatives of the husband cannot be taken into account to sustain the accusations.

12. Considering the submissions made, a fair look at the contents of the complaint would show that this case was lodged on 17.05.2019, vide Cr.No. 84 of 2019 for the offences punishable under Section 498A of IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of the D.P.Act against the petitioners.
According to the respondent No.2, she stayed for three (3) days in in-laws house, and they have continuously tortured her for dowry.
Accused No.1 is a Lt. Commander in Indian Navy.
She again stayed at in laws' house for eight (8) days.
Her in-laws demanded dowry to send her with their son i.e., A1 to Arrakkonam.
She was pressurized by in-laws to take divorce.
After assurance given by her father to fulfill the demand of dowry, Accused No.1 took her to Arrakkonam.
On 25.08.2018, she returned to Visakhapatnam with her father for Rakhi festival.

After few months, in the month of March, 2019, the respondent No.2 along with her father and sister went to Karawar where Accused No.1 is posted to talk to him, where A3 and A4 stated that the respondent No.2 is not up to their VJPJ, standards, they will not accept her unless she gets a flat in Mumbai.
They have not shown any interest to keep the relation.

13. As can be seen from the Judgment in RCSHM/75A/2023 before the Family court, Rewa, Madhya Pradesh, at para 73, it is observed that the respondent No.2 herein as PW1 in cross examination admitted that all the preparations for the marriage were done by A1 and his family members.
There is a finding to the effect that the expenses of the arrangements made for the marriage were borne by the A1 and A3.

At para No.81, there is a finding to the effect that if had the version of the respondent No.2 about the alleged incident within 15 days of the marriage happened, she would have given the complaint to the police but she has not done so.
The learned Judge opined that the said incident was not that serious otherwise her father would not have sent her to her husband's workplace at Arakkonam.
Learned Judge opined that her evidence to that effect is not credible.

Coming to the allegation that Accused No.2, who is the mother in law kept all her jewellery when she left the house Ashutosh Shukla, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75859900/
6 at Mumbai.

sentences.text: It is represented that while leaving the house, the respondent No.2 apart from taking her jewellery, she has also taken the ancestral jewellery from the house.
In that regard, a case has been lodged before the Mumbai Police.

At para 93 of the judgment before the Family Court would show that the respondent No.2 left with her father on 25.08.2018 on invitation of her mother on the festival of Rakshabandhan, had gone to Visakhapatnam.
So the alleged physical and mental cruelty till 25.08.2018 was not believed by the Family Court.
Accordingly, on the point of cruelty, the petition was not VJPJ, considered.

The Court believed the version of the respondent No.2 that A1 deserted her for the period of two years preceding to the filing of the petition, since he had surrendered the Government accommodation which was allotted to him after September, 2018 and before the end November, 2018, that itself speaks about his intention not to continue the matrimonial life with the respondent No.2.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed on the ground of desertion.

The counter claim made by the Accused No.1 seeking divorce against the respondent No.2 on the point of cruelty was rejected but the divorce granted to the wife on the point of desertion under Section 13(1)(1-B) of Hindu Marriage Act.
14. The fact remains that the respondent No.2 stayed with in laws A2 and A3 for a period of six days.
Nothing is there to show that A4 ever stayed with A1 and the respondent No.2, except attending the marriage.
The allegation that they have spent huge amount towards marriage expenses are negatived by the Family court after full trial.
Though the allegations made against the husband A1 on the point of cruelty was not believed by the Family Court, for grant of divorce.
It is needless to say that the term "cruelty" is nowhere defined under Hindu Marriage Act.
Cruelty in one case may not be considered a cruelty in another case.
It is dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case.
The definition of cruelty under 498A of IPC stands on a different footing.
15. A cursory look at the contents of the complaint would show that there are allegations made against the husband in particular about the alleged VJPJ, cruelty.

The finding which was given by the Family Court regarding the allegations made against the Accused Nos. 2 to 4 after full trial would suffice to say that continuing criminal proceedings against them is sheer abuse of process of law.
In the light of discussion referred supra, in the backdrop of the legal position, continuing criminal proceedings against the Accused Nos. 2 to 4 is not tenable.

At this juncture, the learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that Accused No.1 is working at Mumbai, his presence may be dispensed with before the Trial Court since the Court is situated at Visakhapatnam.
16. In the result, the petition is partly allowed.
The criminal proceedings against the Accused Nos. 2 to 4 are quashed.
The presence of the Accused No.1 before the trial court is dispensed with, unless his presence is specifically directed by the Trial Court.
The learned Trial Judge is requested to dispose of the case as expeditiously as possible without granting any adjournment in a casual way on mere asking.
Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.

JUSTICE VENKATA JYOTHIRMAI PRATAPA Date :10.12.2024.
